production.waterSource: Production water comes from springs fed by Taiwan's Snow Mountain and Central Mountain ranges.
production.malt: Malted barley is imported rather than grown in Taiwan; the distillery's regional production material notes imported malt and no in-house malting.
production.fermentation: Temperature-controlled jacketed washbacks are used. Official regional material gives a fermentation period of 3-5 days; established specialist data records 16 closed stainless-steel washbacks and a typical 60-72 hour cycle in current operation.
production.stills: Kavalan uses double distillation in Forsyths copper pot stills. The original configuration used paired 12,000-litre wash stills and 7,000-litre spirit stills; later expansion brought the site to 20 pot stills.
production.maturation: Whisky matures in multi-storey warehouses at Yilan, where strong temperature gradients accelerate extraction. The distillery uses American white oak extensively alongside European wine and sherry casks, with on-site cooperage and STR reconditioning for selected casks.

houseCharacter: Kavalan starts with very soft mountain spring water and temperature-controlled fermentation adapted to Taiwan's subtropical climate. Double distillation in Forsyths copper pot stills creates a clean, fruit-forward new make, while the hot Yilan warehouses accelerate extraction and oxidation. The resulting house style is typically ripe, tropical and cask-expressive, with climate playing a larger role in maturation speed than in traditional cool-climate Scotch production.
cask23Narrative: Kavalan is a useful example of how climate can reshape whisky production without changing the core logic of malt distillation. Mountain spring water, controlled fermentation and Scottish-made copper stills establish a clean spirit, then Taiwan's heat drives unusually active maturation. The result is often intensely fruity and cask-led at younger chronological ages than a drinker might expect from cooler whisky regions.
